proposal.body: Dear Mr Seidl,  Thank you for your quote offer:70740-0 (EUR 6.10, 30 days, 12 months, no index clause). We want to continue the partnership, but this price is well above what we need for a volume award. Your quote:7200008 from 2026-09-09 was EUR 6.06, and our current price is EUR 5.84. We propose a 24-month term, which gives you planning security, with 45 days payment and no index clause at EUR 5.55. The index rose 5.92% in twelve months (idx:AS-14404@2025-09, idx:AS-14404@2026-09), but we would rather settle a fixed price than add volatility. The owner offered to walk us through your calculation. Could you share the material and hourly-rate breakdown so we can find where the gap sits? Best regards, Hollerau Pumpenwerke Purchasing
Thank you for your offer. We need a better price to go ahead.

Dear Mr Seidl,  Thank you for your quotation of EUR 6.10, 30 days, 12 months, no index clause. We would like to build a longer partnership at our full volume of 23,700 kg a year, but the price is well above where we need to be. To help us find a workable package, could you send three alternatives across unit price, payment days, contract term and index clause: an opening, an improved and a best-final package? Please also share your calculation (material and hourly rates) so we understand your cost drivers. To show our intent, we can discuss a 24-month term and faster payment in exchange for a clearly lower base price. We would also like to understand which index structure you consider fair. Kind regards, AEIOU, Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke

proposal.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your revised quotation and for accepting the 36-month term and the AS-14404 index clause. We appreciate the movement and your confirmation that the order-price history holds.

We understand that your costs have risen over the past year. The most recent index window points the other way: AS-14404 changed by -5.49% from 2026-06 to 2026-09 (idx:AS-14404@2026-06, idx:AS-14404@2026-09). We recognise that this sits alongside the annual rise you described.

On that basis, would you kindly consider EUR 4.72/kg for part:370010? The package would be payment within 30 days net, a 36-month contract, and AS-14404 on a 45% material share with a 0% deadband and base month 2026-08. The fixed terms are unchanged: 23,700 kg per year, DAP, a 14-day lead time, effective 2027-01-01 and no tooling charges.

Could you let us know whether you can approve this as a binding offer?

Kind regards,
Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke

Thank you for working through the options with us. We appreciate your team's careful review and would like to find an arrangement that works for Werdenfels as well as for us.

Could you kindly consider one of these complete alternatives? Each price is conditional on its payment term and adjustment clause.

Option A: EUR 5.07/kg, payment within 30 days net, a 36-month contract, AS-14404 on a 45% material share, 5% deadband and base month 2026-08.
Option B: EUR 5.05/kg, payment within 14 days net, a 36-month contract, AS-14404 on a 45% material share, 5% deadband and base month 2026-08.
Option C: EUR 5.10/kg, payment within 60 days net, a 36-month contract, AS-14404 on a 45% material share, 5% deadband and base month 2026-08.

The fixed terms of our enquiry remain unchanged. These are new proposals for your approval. Could you issue the option you can approve as your binding offer? If none works, which term would need to change? We would be pleased to review it together.

Kind regards,
Purchasing

proposal.body:
Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for building on Option A. We appreciate your team keeping the 36-month term, the AS-14404 clause with a 5% deadband and the 30-day payment, and the movement you have made on price.

Since we now seem aligned on the structure, the remaining difference is the price. For your review, AS-14404 changed by -5.49% from 2026-06 to 2026-09 (idx:AS-14404@2026-06, idx:AS-14404@2026-09). We recognise that this recent window can coexist with the annual increase you described. The proposed clause would continue to reflect AS-14404 movements beyond the deadband over the contract term.

Could you kindly review whether you can approve Option A as your binding offer? Option A is EUR 5.07/kg, payment within 30 days net, a 36-month contract, AS-14404 on a 45% material share, 5% deadband and base month 2026-08. The fixed terms of our enquiry stay unchanged. If the price is what prevents approval, could your pricing committee review this complete package?

Kind regards,
Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke

Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for your revised offer and for moving to EUR 5.20/kg with 14-day payment. We appreciate the step and your flexibility on the payment terms.

Building on the structure you proposed, we would like to ask your team to approve EUR 5.05/kg, payment within 14 days net, a 36-month contract, AS-14404 on a 45% material share, 5% deadband and base month 2026-08. The fixed terms of our enquiry remain unchanged. This is a new proposal for your approval, not an agreed position.

On the alloy component, AS-14404 changed by -5.49% from 2026-06 to 2026-09 (idx:AS-14404@2026-06, idx:AS-14404@2026-09). We recognise that this recent window can coexist with the annual increase you described. The AS-14404 clause would also adjust the price if the series moves beyond the deadband during the contract.

Could the colleague authorised to approve the complete package issue it as your binding offer? If a specific term stands in the way, please tell us which one, and we will gladly review it with you.

Kind regards,
Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke

Dear Mr Seidl,

Thank you for building on Option A and for moving to the 5% deadband. We appreciate your team's work on this and the progress we have made together.

We now agree on the structure: 36 months, 30 days net and AS-14404 on a 45% material share with a 5% deadband and base month 2026-08. The remaining gap is the starting price.

For your review, AS-14404 changed by -5.49% from 2026-06 to 2026-09 (idx:AS-14404@2026-06, idx:AS-14404@2026-09). We recognise that this recent movement can coexist with the annual rise you described. The agreed clause will also protect Werdenfels if alloy costs move beyond the deadband.

Could you approve Option A as your binding offer: EUR 5.07/kg, payment within 30 days net, a 36-month contract and the clause above? The fixed terms of our enquiry remain unchanged. Option C, at EUR 5.10/kg with payment within 60 days net and the same clause, also remains open to you.

Kind regards,
Purchasing, Hollerau Pumpenwerke
